The pattern (Wed 2025-10-29, Wed 2024-10-30) points to Wed Oct 28 or Thu Oct 29, before the Oct 30 scoring close. It is the first print on the new Agents and Infra / Devices and Consumer segments. fair_value.method: 65% forward P/E: core FY28 EPS $23.0 x 24x = $552, plus the OpenAI stake at about $27/share, gives $579. 35% DCF: lease-adjusted FCF margins 5% in FY27 rising to 27% by FY32, 8.5% WACC, 3.5% terminal growth, net debt of $33B including finance leases, plus the OpenAI stake, gives $470. The blend is about $541 per share at Sept 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Core FY28 (June-2028) non-GAAP EPS $23.0 x 24x ex-OpenAI multiple = $552, plus 25% OpenAI stake at about $1.1T less 27% tax/illiquidity haircut = about $27/share

inputs_detail.derivation: Excludes OpenAI investment impacts of $0.67; GAAP EPS was $17.95. The core EPS therefore excludes the OpenAI equity-method result, so the stake is valued separately.

This is 2.5-3% below the $23.57-23.68 consensus. The haircut covers server depreciation (2-6 year lives) and operating-lease cost from the $329.1B of uncommenced datacenter leases starting FY27-FY33 [2]. FY27 capex is guided to grow year on year from FY26's roughly $140B ($116B cash PP&E plus $24.6B of finance-lease additions [2]) [4]. The building useful-life change (15 to 25 years) gives only a 'minimal benefit to FY27 operating income' [4], so it is not a cushion. FY27 operating margin is guided down less than 1pt [4]. That caps the haircut: a deeper cut is not backed by guidance.

Spot is 26.2x FY27 and about 22x FY28 consensus [6,7]. That spot multiple includes whatever the market credits for the OpenAI stake, about $27/share or 1.5 turns. Round 1 used 25x including the stake. I now use 24x on core earnings and add the stake separately (net about +$4/share versus round 1). 24x is below the historical 28-32x because FCF yield is compressed during the build-out and about 40% of RPO is concentrated in OpenAI, which can now use other clouds [11].

The 10-K states an 'approximate 25% interest on an as-converted basis' [2]. At the $852B March round [12] that is $213B, and at the reported ~$1.4T talks [13] it is $350B. I use a $1.1T midpoint = $275B, less 27% for tax and illiquidity (no 2026 IPO), = about $200B / 7.43B shares. $11.9B of $13.0B committed funding is already paid [2].

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Revenue FY27 $391B, then $465B / $540B / $615B / $689B / $758B to FY32. Lease-adjusted FCF margins 5%, 7%, 12%, 18%, 24%, 27%. WACC 8.5%, terminal growth 3.5%, valued at Sept 2027. EV $3.31T less $33B net debt including finance leases (core $443/share), plus OpenAI stake $200B, over 7.40B shares = $470

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY28 revenue is $467B [7]. Support: commercial RPO of $678B (+84%; about 30% recognized within 12 months) [2]. Ex-OpenAI RPO grew +25% and all sequential RPO growth was non-frontier [4].

This is 2-3pt below round 1 in FY27-FY29. The call says ~$175B is the calendar-2026 capex expectation after moving more future datacenter leases from finance to operating treatment, and that FY27 capex will grow year on year [4]. The lease shift flatters reported capex and FCF, while operating-lease payments start running through OCF on the $329.1B uncommenced leases [2]. Consensus FY27/FY28 FCF is $32B/$46B [7]. Margins normalize toward the pre-AI ~30% by FY32.
AAA issuer with low funded debt ($46.1B face). Equity risk is raised by $744B of contractual obligations and ~40% OpenAI concentration in RPO [2,14].

Cash and short-term investments $76.8B, minus debt $46.1B face, minus finance lease liabilities $66.6B = -$35.9B at face (-$30B at book debt of $40.3B). I use the midpoint, about $33B. Operating lease liabilities ($21.9B) are excluded because their cost runs through FCF. Round 1 used +$30.7B net cash, which ignored finance leases.
Same as in the P/E method. Microsoft's own FCF excludes it.

bear.story: AI capex payback disappoints. OpenAI, about 40% of the $678B RPO and $24.1B (7.3%) of FY26 revenue, shifts incremental workloads to other clouds under the April 2026 amendment or re-prices its commitments. Azure decelerates into the 20s as capacity catches up. FY27 capex grows beyond the CY26 ~$175B while operating-lease costs from $329B of uncommenced leases hit margins by more than the guided <1pt. Core FY28 EPS is about $21 at about 17x, plus a marked-down OpenAI stake of about $15/share.

base.story: Azure grows 35-45% through FY27 while still capacity-constrained. Ex-OpenAI RPO keeps compounding at about 25%. M365 commercial cloud grows about 17% cc. Operating margin dips less than 1pt as guided. Core FY28 EPS of about $23 at 23.5x ($540), plus the OpenAI stake of about $27-30.

bull.story: Capex converts quickly: agentic products monetize, non-frontier bookings broaden, and Microsoft Cloud gross margin holds. Core FY28 EPS reaches about $24.5 at about 28x as FCF inflects in FY28. The OpenAI stake is marked at $1.4T+ (about $45/share net).

thesis_break_reason: At $400, net of the roughly $27/share OpenAI stake, the core business would trade at about $373, or about 16x my $23.0 core FY28 EPS (about 17x including the stake). That would likely mean the market has concluded the AI build will not earn its cost of capital. Scale of the build: FY27 capex growing beyond FY26's roughly $140B including finance leases, CY26 ~$175B, and $329B of uncommenced leases. Concrete triggers: OpenAI moving or re-pricing its roughly $270-280B RPO commitment under its any-cloud rights, Azure below about 30%, or operating margin guided down well beyond 1pt. The stock touched $349 in 2026 with earnings intact, so I would confirm a break with estimate cuts, not price alone.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's fact-checks, verified against primary documents where possible, corrected four inputs. (1) Capex period. The Q4 FY26 call [4] says the ~$175B is the calendar-2026 capex expectation, lowered only because future datacenter leases shift from finance to operating treatment, and that 'FY27 capital expenditures will grow year-over-year'. The recap bullet I had relied on mislabelled it as FY27. FY26 capex including finance leases was about $140B ($116B cash PP&E plus $24.6B finance-lease additions, 10-K [2]). I cut DCF FCF margins by 2-3pt in FY27-FY29 so the lease reclassification does not flatter them. (2) Net debt. The 10-K shows $66.6B of finance lease liabilities, so net debt including them is about $30-36B, not +$30.7B net cash. That is about -$9/share in the DCF. (3) The OpenAI stake (10-K: ~25% as-converted; related-party revenue $24.1B; $11.9B of $13.0B funded) is now valued separately at about $27/share, and I cut the core P/E multiple from 25x to 24x so the stake is not double-counted. (4) OpenAI is about 40% of RPO (bounded by the Dec-2025 45% of $625B plus non-frontier sequential growth) and can use any cloud (April 2026 blog [11]). That concentration fattens my bear case: bear price $390 to $385, and the bear multiple is lower. The corrections mostly offset. The P/E leg rose from $575 to $579 (stake +$27, multiple -$23). The DCF was essentially flat, $473 to $470 (lower FCF and net debt, offset by the stake). Blended fair value is $541 versus $540. Scenario mean is about $563 (25/50/25 at $385 / $570 / $725). The ladder is centered on a median of about $548 (about 6% drift including the 0.7% dividend) at about 31% vol, with a slightly heavier left tail for the concentration and capex risk. P(>=518) goes from 0.585 to 0.578. Where I differ from the supervisor: I do not subtract net debt in the P/E leg, because interest and finance-lease cost are already in EPS, and my stake haircut (27%) is a bit larger than its 25%. Research this round was 5 fetches: the call transcript, the 10-K lease/related-party/cash-flow notes, and the IR event page (404). The $852B/$1.4T OpenAI marks and the Dec-2025 RPO share are taken from the supervisor's cited sources, not re-read.
